newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Hashimoto, Suharto discuss Indonesia car policy.
newsitem.headline: Hashimoto, Suharto discuss Indonesia car policy.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto discussed the nation's controversial national car policy with Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Friday and both agreed it would not harm bilateral ties, an official said.
"President Suharto explained the background of the national car policy," State Secretary Murdiono told reporters after a 90-minute meeting between the two leaders.

Japanese diplomats had said ahead of Hashimoto's arrival in Jakarta on Thursday that the prime minister would not bring up controversial issues such as the car policy and human rights in East Timor in talks with Suharto.

Japan, the United States and the European Union have challenged Indonesia at the World Trade Organisation over its decision to give tariff breaks to a company headed by one of Suharto's sons to produce a national car in association with a South Korean firm.
Murdiono said Suharto maintained that Indonesia, as an archipelagic state, needed to be self-sufficient in its production of transportation equipment.
"In the long term, to produce transportation equipment is part of the national policy," he quoted the president as saying.
"The president explained that the national car policy in cooperation with South Korea does not mean discrimination against other countries," Murdiono said.

"The prime minister said that Japan can understand and support Indonesia in making its own car, but Japan is of the opinion that the national car policy had to be carried out in accordance with existing international agreeements or the World Trade Organisation.
"However, both leaders agreed the car issue will not disturb good bilateral relations between the two countries," the State Secretary added.
Japan is Indonesia's biggest trading partner and biggest aid donor. Japanese investment in Indonesia rose to nearly $7.0 billion in 1996 from $3.8 billion in 1995.
Indonesia is Japan's third-largest foreign source of oil and natural gas.

Hashimoto is on his first official tour of five Southeast Asian nations. He visited Malaysia before arriving in Indonesia and will leave for Vietnam on Saturday. Hashimoto will also be visiting Brunei and Singapore.
